biography: Ni Amorim, born in the bustling port city of Porto, Portugal, wasn't raised in a racing family. His passion ignited unexpectedly at age 16, witnessing a local hill climb event where a beat-up Lancia Delta Integrale roared past, captivating his soul. He started with karting, scraping together money from odd jobs to buy a used kart. His raw talent was undeniable, but his aggressive style often led to crashes and near misses. After a few regional karting championships, he caught the eye of a small GT team, launching his career in GT racing. A defining moment was his unexpected podium finish at the Estoril GT round in 2018, showcasing his wet-weather prowess. Now, at 35, his career is on the decline, struggling to secure top drives, but his fiery spirit remains.
drivingStyle: Amorim is known for his relentlessly aggressive driving style. He attacks corners with a 'no-holds-barred' approach, often pushing the limits of grip and flirting with disaster. Tire management is not his forte; he tends to overdrive the car early in stints, sacrificing long-run pace for initial speed. However, his aggressive nature makes him a formidable opponent in wheel-to-wheel combat, especially under pressure. He thrives in chaotic races where his daring overtakes and uncompromising attitude can make the difference.
rivalries: Marco Bellini: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision at the 2019 Monza GT race, where Bellini accused Amorim of deliberately taking him out.
Isabelle Moreau: A clash of personalities and driving styles, with Moreau's calculated precision often at odds with Amorim's impulsive aggression.
Kenji Tanaka: Their rivalry ignited in junior formulas, a battle between Amorim's raw talent and Tanaka's meticulous preparation.
quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks, threadbare as they may be, for every race.
Listens to fado music (a melancholic genre of Portuguese music) to calm his nerves before a race.
Refuses to shake hands with anyone on the grid before the start, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about poetry; it's about war. And I intend to win every battle.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in 2020 with Milano GT36, a hard-fought victory achieved through relentless driving and strategic brilliance from the team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2021 Nürburgring 24 Hours, costing his team a certain victory and earning him widespread criticism.
